mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 98 for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO < 98.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in RSAFS below the 10th percentile for the past year indicates a tightening monetary policy coupled with reduced consumer savings, which constrains spending and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising AND RSAFS < 10th percentile for 12 months
regime_hint: monetary tightening with reduced household savings
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is rising and RSAFS is below its 10th percentile for 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in HOUST and GDPC1 above their respective 3-month moving averages signals strengthening housing demand and overall economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and GDPC1 are above their 3-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decrease in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS is below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for the previous six months signals an unexpected inflation surge with accommodative policy, which erodes real earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% in one month AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for previous six months
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with inflation surprise
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL jumps above 4% and FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for six months prior.
